title: Driver-native tenant scope hides platform-global (NULL-org) rows from an org-context read (sys_license: admin sees 0, anon sees row)
body:
## Symptom On the cloud control plane (`apps/cloud`), a **platform admin who also owns an org** reads `sys_license` and gets **0 rows**, while the row exists in the control DB and an **unauthenticated** request to the same endpoint returns it. ``` row in control DB : lic_… (organization_id = NULL, signed_token present) anon GET /api/v1/data/sys_license → 1 row admin GET /api/v1/data/sys_license → { records: [], total: 0 } ← bug ``` `sys_license` is declared `tenancy: { enabled: false }` + `access: { default: 'private' }` + `requiredPermissions: ['manage_platform_settings']` (ADR-0066). The admin holds the capability and passes the CRUD + requiredPermissions gates (HTTP 200, not 403) — they just get **0 rows**. ## What is NOT the cause (ruled out by tracing) - **Not the ADR-0066 authz kernel / RLS.** plugin-security applies **no** row filter for the admin — traced `astWhere = undefined` in the security middleware. requiredPermissions/RLS are correct. - **Not the objectos KernelResolver.** Instrumented `createCloudKernelResolver.resolveKernel` (console.error at the top) → **0 hits** in both cloud.log and objectos.log for the read. apps/cloud runs no env kernels. - **Not the runtime http-dispatcher.** Instrumented `HttpDispatcher.callData` → **0 hits**. apps/cloud serves data via **`@objectstack/rest` (`rest-server.ts`)**, whose `resolveProtocol(undefined)` returns the **control-plane protocol** for both admin and anon. So admin and anon hit the **same** control-plane protocol / engine / driver, with the **same unfiltered query** (`astWhere=undefined`), yet get different results. The only difference is the execution context's `tenantId`. ## Root cause — engine/driver-native tenant scope (separate from RLS) The tenant `WHERE` is injected **below** plugin-security: - **`packages/objectql/src/engine.ts:805`** — `buildDriverOptions` copies the request tenant into driver options: ```ts if (hasTenant && opts.tenantId === undefined) { opts.tenantId = execCtx!.tenantId; } ``` Admin → `opts.tenantId = `; anon → `tenantId` undefined (no scope). - **`packages/plugins/driver-sql/src/sql-driver.ts:2764` `applyTenantScope`** (called from `find`/`findOne`, lines 691/776): ```ts const tenantId = options?.tenantId; if (tenantId == null || tenantId === '') return builder; // anon: no scope → sees the row const field = this.resolveTenantField(object); // ← the crux if (!field) return builder; return builder.where(b => b.where(field, String(tenantId)).orWhereNull(field)); // (#2734) ``` `resolveTenantField` reads a **cached** `tenantFieldByTable[table]` (2728), populated at registration from `computeTenantField` (1965), which **does** honor the posture: ```ts if (tenancyDecl?.enabled === false) return null; // 1968 — correct if (fields has 'organization_id') return 'organization_id'; // 1974 — default heuristic ``` So the intended behavior is: `sys_license` (tenancy disabled) ⇒ `computeTenantField` → `null` ⇒ **no tenant scope** ⇒ admin sees the row. It doesn't happen, so one of: 1. **Stale / mis-timed `tenantFieldByTable` cache** — `sys_license`'s table was registered (and its tenant field cached as `organization_id`, via the 1974 heuristic on its `organization_id` lookup column) **before** the `tenancy.enabled:false` posture propagated to the driver, and the cache is never invalidated. `resolveTenantField('sys_license')` then returns `organization_id` despite the posture. 2. **Global-row (`orWhereNull`) rule missing on the running build** — if `applyTenantScope` used strict equality (pre-#2734) rather than `field = tenantId OR field IS NULL`, an org-context read excludes the NULL-org row. (Current `main` has the `orWhereNull`; if it's applied, the NULL-org row *should* survive even when scoped — so (1) is the more likely primary cause, with a real-column mismatch.) ## Definitive one-line probe ```ts // sql-driver.ts applyTenantScope, top: if (object === 'sys_license') console.error('[TSCOPE]', { object, tenantId: (options as any)?.tenantId, field: this.resolveTenantField(object) }); ``` Read `sys_license` as admin vs anon and compare `field`. Expected finding: admin has `tenantId=` and `field='organization_id'` (posture not honored at the driver) → the row is scoped out. ## Fix options - **Framework (root cause):** make `resolveTenantField` reflect the object's **live** posture — recompute/invalidate `tenantFieldByTable` when a schema registers with `tenancy.enabled:false` (or resolve `computeTenantField` from the current registered schema rather than a one-time cache). Then a platform-global object is never tenant-scoped. Also keep the `orWhereNull` global-row inclusion (#2734) as defense-in-depth so NULL-org rows survive any legitimate scope. - **ADR-0066 alignment:** the driver tenant-scope decision should treat `access:{default:'private'}` / `tenancy.enabled:false` as platform-global (never org-scoped) — the same posture the authz kernel already honors. - **Cloud mitigation (optional):** apps/cloud need not stamp `execCtx.tenantId` for control-plane object reads. ## Repro (local stack) `CLOUD_PORT=

OBJECTOS_PORT= OS_LICENSE_PRIVATE_KEY_PEM= bash scripts/dev-local/run-stack.sh --with-ui --prod-like --seed --keep`, issue a license as `admin@local.test`, then `GET /api/v1/data/sys_license` as the admin (0) vs anon (1). Surfaced while implementing ADR-0066 (secure-by-default `sys_license`); the authz kernel itself is correct — this is the pre-existing engine/driver tenant-scope layer.
